title: Monic finite coordinate chart at a nonzero polynomial prime
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge1$, $A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and $0\ne\mathfrak q\subset A$ a prime ideal. Fix $0\ne g\in\mathfrak q$. Polynomial rings are as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exist positive integers $e_i$ for $i<n$, a nonzero scalar $a\in k$, and $d>0$ such that the $k$-algebra automorphism $\sigma:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ given by $\sigma(x_i)=x_i+x_n^{e_i}$ for $i<n$ and $\sigma(x_n)=x_n$ has inverse $x_i\mapsto x_i-x_n^{e_i}$, and $f=a^{-1}\sigma(g)$ is monic of degree $d$ in $x_n$. Put $\mathfrak q^*=\sigma(\mathfrak q)$, $B=k[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}]$, $C=B[y_n]$, and define $\psi:C\to A$ by $\psi(y_i)=x_i$ for $i<n$ and $\psi(y_n)=f$. Then $\mathfrak q^*$ is prime, $f\in\mathfrak q^*$, and $\psi$ is finite: $1,x_n,\ldots,x_n^{d-1}$ generate $A$ as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The ideal $\mathfrak p=(\psi|_B)^{-1}(\mathfrak q^*)$ is prime and $$\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q^*)=\mathfrak pC+(y_n).$$ More explicitly, for every $H\in C$, $\psi(H)\in\mathfrak q^*$ if and only if $H(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1},0)\in\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: Since $\mathfrak q$ is proper, $g$ cannot be a nonzero constant: such a constant is a unit in $A$, and its membership would imply $1\in\mathfrak q$. Since $g\ne0$, it is therefore nonconstant. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-shear-leading-coefficient] with $R=k$ to obtain positive $e_i$, $d>0$, $a\ne0$, and $b_j\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$ with $g(x_1+x_n^{e_1},\ldots,x_{n-1}+x_n^{e_{n-1}},x_n)=a x_n^d+\sum_{j<d}b_jx_n^j$.

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, proof: nonzero-prime step before induction; Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial.

proof.text: By the evaluation universal property of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], define $\sigma$ by the displayed substitutions and $\tau$ by $x_i\mapsto x_i-x_n^{e_i}$ for $i<n$, fixing $x_n$. Both composites fix every generator: $(x_i-x_n^{e_i})+x_n^{e_i}=x_i$ and $(x_i+x_n^{e_i})-x_n^{e_i}=x_i$, since both maps fix $x_n$. They also fix $k$, so uniqueness gives $\sigma\tau=\tau\sigma=1$. Thus $\sigma$ is the required automorphism. As $a\in k^\times$, setting $c_j=a^{-1}b_j$ gives $f=a^{-1}\sigma(g)=x_n^d+\sum_{j<d}c_jx_n^j$, monic of degree $d$.

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, proof: nonzero-prime step before induction; Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial.

proof.text: The image $\mathfrak q^*=\sigma(\mathfrak q)$ is an ideal: applying $\tau$ reduces addition and multiplication by an arbitrary element to the ideal axioms for $\mathfrak q$. It is proper since $\tau(1)=1\notin\mathfrak q$. If $uv\in\mathfrak q^*$, then $\tau(u)\tau(v)\in\mathfrak q$, so one factor belongs to $\mathfrak q$, and hence $u$ or $v$ belongs to $\mathfrak q^*$. This proves primality. Moreover $\sigma(g)\in\mathfrak q^*$, so $f=a^{-1}\sigma(g)\in\mathfrak q^*$.

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, proof: nonzero-prime step before induction; Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial.

proof.text: Let $\iota:B\to A$ send $y_i$ to $x_i$, and define $\psi:B[y_n]\to A$ by $\psi|_B=\iota$ and $\psi(y_n)=f$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For each $c_j$ choose the identical coefficient polynomial $\widetilde c_j\in B$ with $\iota(\widetilde c_j)=c_j$. We have the explicit relation $$x_n^d=\psi(y_n)-\sum_{j<d}\psi(\widetilde c_j)x_n^j.$$ Strong induction on $m\ge0$ shows $x_n^m$ lies in the $C$-span of $1,\ldots,x_n^{d-1}$. For $m<d$ this is a generator. For $m\ge d$, multiply the relation by $x_n^{m-d}$; it expresses $x_n^m$ as $\psi(y_n)x_n^{m-d}-\sum_{j<d}\psi(\widetilde c_j)x_n^{m-d+j}$. Every exponent on the right is less than $m$ since $d>0$ and $j<d$, so the induction applies. Grouping monomials of any element of $A$ by their $x_n$ exponent writes it as $\sum_m\iota(h_m)x_n^m$ with $h_m\in B$, a finite sum. Substituting the preceding expressions proves that the displayed $d$ elements generate $A$ as a $C$-module. This is precisely finiteness in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, proof: nonzero-prime step before induction; Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial.

proof.text: Define $\mathfrak p=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q^*)$. Preimages preserve the ideal axioms. It is proper since $\iota(1)=1\notin\mathfrak q^*$; if $uv\in\mathfrak p$, then $\iota(u)\iota(v)\in\mathfrak q^*$, so the primality established in Step 3 implies $u\in\mathfrak p$ or $v\in\mathfrak p$. For $H=\sum_{j=0}^N h_jy_n^j\in C$, evaluation gives $\psi(H)=\iota(h_0)+f\sum_{j=1}^N\iota(h_j)f^{j-1}$. Since $f\in\mathfrak q^*$, this belongs to $\mathfrak q^*$ exactly when $\iota(h_0)\in\mathfrak q^*$, equivalently $h_0=H(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1},0)\in\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, proof: nonzero-prime step before induction; Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial.

proof.text: Finally $H=h_0+y_n\sum_{j=1}^N h_jy_n^{j-1}$. If $h_0\in\mathfrak p$, this expression puts $H$ in $\mathfrak pC+(y_n)$. Conversely, evaluating at $y_n=0$ sends a finite sum of multiples of elements of $\mathfrak p$ into $\mathfrak p$, and sends every multiple of $y_n$ to zero. Thus membership in $\mathfrak pC+(y_n)$ is equivalent to $H(0)\in\mathfrak p$. Combining with Step 5 proves $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q^*)=\mathfrak pC+(y_n)$ and the asserted explicit criterion. When $n=1$, $B=k$ and the shear lists are empty; all these formulas and the induction remain valid.
